references.text: Fulfillment of the sign: Moses strikes the water in the Nile with his staff, and it turns to blood. This is the first plague upon Egypt.
The two preceding signs that God gave Moses: the staff turning into a snake and the hand becoming leprous. The verse refers to these as 'the two signs'.
Moses uses his staff again at the Nile water, this time to strike the rock at Horeb to give the Israelites water.
The psalmist recalls how God turned the rivers of Egypt into blood so that they could not drink.
The psalm describes how God turned the waters of Egypt into blood and killed their fish.
In Revelation, bowls of wrath are poured out, and the sea and rivers turn to blood, echoing the plagues in Egypt.
The two witnesses have power to turn water into blood, like Moses' sign in Egypt.
This is the instruction given to Moses about the sign that is later carried out in 7:18.
Ezekiel expands the motif of drying up the Nile from a single sign in Exodus into a prophecy of national destruction.
Theological contrast: water on dry land as judgment in Exodus versus the pouring out of the Spirit as blessing in Isaiah.
